page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 96 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multi-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is compatible with Premium Storage options.

Benchmark evaluations place the D96as_v7 in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance. Its memory subsystem demonstrates strong capabilities, achieving a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 9446.68 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 174.77 GB/sec. In database operations, the server processed 138.89 million Redis SET operations per second, ranking in the top 10% of tested hardware. Cryptographic and compression tests, including Passmark CPU encryption and bzip3 decompression, also consistently scored in the top tier.

For artificial intelligence workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds across small, medium, and large language models, though prompt processing for large 70B models drops to an average tier of 25.78 tokens/sec. Given the high-density compute resources and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D96as_v7 is suited for enterprise-grade web serving, relational database hosting, large-scale data compression, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
